registeredBy: Sam (owner); registered before any run of this version
hypothesis: With an output gap in the rule, when the policy rate sits more than 1 point above it (tight) the central bank cuts within 6 months more often than in any month, and when it sits more than 1 point below (loose) it hikes within 6 months more often than in any month; the edge survives counting cases in the same year as one block and holds in most countries.

retestOf.verdict: failed (61 of 161 = 37.9% against 34.8%, lift 3.1 points, p 0.23)
retestOf.change: Adds the output-gap term of Taylor (1993), 0.5 x gap, that version 1 left out and listed as its first known limit. The gap is the app's real-time estimate (one-sided Hodrick-Prescott, lambda 100, on IMF real GDP growth outturns up to each year), and year t is used only from April of t+1. Everything else is as in version 1, and the verdict is by method 2.

knownLimits: Re-test of a failed rule: version 1 failed, and this version was written after seeing that result. The change is the term version 1 named as missing, with the textbook weight, not a weight chosen to fit.
The output gap is annual and lagged: in a month of year t+1 before April, the latest gap is for year t-1. Gaps from GDP alone are rough and the newest year moves most.
GDP growth and inflation are today's vintages: the filter uses only past years, but revisions to past data are not undone.
Neutral real rate fixed at 2% for every country, as in version 1; emerging markets with higher neutral rates read loose more often.
Same dated target table, exclusions (Turkey, pegs, no numeric target) and first-month-of-run calls as version 1.
